summary: Extend the existing vanilla-JS frontend baseline instead of rebuilding it. The workspace already supports clipboard parsing, 6 compact candidate previews, candidate selection, and two-click swap editing. This iteration should preserve that behavior, add editable per-player role preferences, localStorage-backed saved player records and exact-10 loading, and surface preference-fit metadata without exposing numeric scores. The older real-browser/mobile smoke gap stays documented but is non-blocking for this round.

milestones.title: Canonical Match State
milestones.objective: Refactor the app so a structured current-match roster, not raw textarea text alone, becomes the source of truth for preferences, saved-player hydration, candidate generation, and editor loading.
deliverables: Extend `src/types.ts` with explicit shapes for `preferenceOrder`, `preferenceSource`, `MatchPlayer`, and `SavedPlayerRecord` so the data model is stable before UI work starts.
Add a small helper module such as `src/lib/preferences.js` for default-order derivation, unique-order normalization, and assigned-role-to-preference-rank calculation.
Add `src/lib/playerStore.js` as a versioned `localStorage` wrapper with safe JSON parsing, empty-store fallback, and upsert-by-normalized-name behavior.

Refactor `src/main.js` and `src/lib/appFlow.js` so `matchPlayers` is the canonical state; textarea paste and saved-player load both hydrate that array, and balance/editor flows read it directly instead of reparsing raw text during every interaction.

Keep `src/lib/parseClipboard.js` behavior unchanged for the existing 4-column TSV format with optional header support; when a pasted name already exists in storage, hydrate saved preference order but keep pasted tier values as the current-match truth.

milestones.title: Preference Editing Workflow
milestones.objective: Let the user input or change each player's role preference order in a simple Korean UI without changing the clipboard format.
deliverables: Update `src/lib/render.js`, `src/constants/copy.js`, and `src/styles.css` so the current-roster area shows the 10 active players with tier chips plus compact `1순위 / 2순위 / 3순위` role controls per row.

Use a deterministic default preference order when none exists yet: highest tier score first, with ties resolved `tank -> damage -> support`, so pasted players are immediately usable before manual edits.
Enforce unique role order in the controls through shared normalization logic; do not allow duplicate roles in the same player's preference list.

Extend candidate/editor assignment data in `src/lib/optimizer.js` and `src/lib/editor.js` with `preferenceRank` metadata so each visible slot can show `1순위`, `2순위`, or `3순위`/mismatch state for the assigned role.
Recalculate preference badges immediately after candidate selection or slot swaps, while keeping all numeric score values hidden from the main UI.

milestones.title: Saved Player Library
milestones.objective: Persist player tiers and preferences locally and let the user assemble a match by choosing exactly 10 saved players.
deliverables: Add a `현재 10명 저장/업데이트` action that persists the current valid roster into `localStorage` as reusable saved-player records.
Add a saved-player panel that renders on startup and lists stored players with name, tier summary, preference summary, and a selection checkbox.
Track saved-player selection count in app state and enable `선택한 10명 불러오기` only when exactly 10 players are checked.

When 10 saved players are loaded, rewrite the textarea with canonical TSV including a header row, hydrate `matchPlayers`, refresh the current-roster preview, and clear old candidates/editor until the user recalculates.
Update Korean UI copy so role preferences and saved players are presented as supported workflow, not as out-of-scope nice-to-have text.

milestones.title: Result Integration And Verification
milestones.objective: Integrate the new metadata into the existing candidate/swap flow and lock the release with deterministic tests and docs.
deliverables: Preserve the current result behavior: 6 compact candidate cards, fixed `1탱 2딜 2힐` slot structure, default first-candidate selection, and two-click cross-team/cross-role swaps.

Keep the mandatory candidate ordering unchanged in `src/lib/optimizer.js`: total score difference, role-score-difference sum, tank score difference, then unranked difference; role preferences may be displayed as fit metadata but must not override that sort order.
If space allows, add a compact candidate-level preference-fit summary, but do not surface personal score, team total score, or numeric score differences anywhere in the main UI.
Extend `testing/fakeDom.js` with the minimum support needed for the new controls, especially `localStorage`, checkbox state, select/input value changes, and the related event dispatch behavior.

Add tests for preference defaults and edits, localStorage save/load/upsert, exact-10 saved-player loading, preference-rank recalculation after swaps, hidden-score UI, and unchanged parser/ranking behavior.

Run `npm test` and `npm run build` as mandatory verification. Keep `npm run test:browser` optional only when a Chromium-family browser exists, and document clearly that this round does not treat the older browser/mobile gap as a blocker.
Update `README.md` and `FINAL_OUTPUT.md` so setup, supported workflow, verification evidence, and remaining non-blocking QA gaps all match the shipped behavior.

acceptance_criteria: Header-present and headerless 4-column paste input both still parse correctly and keep Korean validation errors for bad input.
The current-roster view shows all 10 active players with tier presentation and editable unique `1순위 / 2순위 / 3순위` role preferences.
If a player has no stored or manually edited preference order yet, the app derives a default order from highest tier score, with ties resolved `tank -> damage -> support`.
Saving the current valid roster creates or updates localStorage records keyed by normalized player name.
Reloading the app restores the saved-player list from localStorage without any backend dependency.
The saved-player panel keeps `선택한 10명 불러오기` disabled unless exactly 10 saved players are selected.
Loading 10 saved players repopulates the textarea and current-roster preview with those exact 10 players and their saved preferences.
After valid current players exist, the app still shows exactly 6 candidate combinations.
Every candidate still satisfies `1탱 2딜 2힐` per team and does not duplicate any player within that candidate.
Candidate ordering still follows total score difference, role-score-difference sum, tank score difference, then unranked difference.
Candidate preview cards remain compact and show both `팀 A` and `팀 B` slot layouts with required tier color styling.
Candidate previews and the final editor visibly reflect each assignment's role-preference rank or mismatch state.
Selecting a candidate still loads a fresh final edit area for that candidate and clears any previous pending swap selection.
Two slot clicks still swap players immediately across teams or roles, and after the swap both tier display and preference rank are recalculated from the destination slot role.
The main UI still hides personal numeric scores, team total scores, and numeric score differences by default.
All newly added product copy for preference editing and saved players is in Korean.
`README.md` and `FINAL_OUTPUT.md` describe the preference/save workflow and state that the older browser/mobile smoke gap is non-blocking for this iteration.
test_strategy: Add pure unit tests for the new preference helper module covering default-order derivation, duplicate-order normalization, and assigned-role-to-preference-rank mapping.
Add storage tests for the new `localStorage` wrapper covering empty state, corrupted JSON fallback, upsert-by-name updates, and round-trip persistence.
Keep optimizer tests focused on the required balance ordering and candidate uniqueness so preference metadata cannot silently change ranking behavior.
Extend editor tests so swaps assert both destination-role tier recalculation and destination-role preference-rank recalculation.

Expand the fake-DOM app-flow tests to cover preference editing, saving the current roster, restoring saved players on startup, exact-10 selection gating, loading saved players into the textarea/preview, candidate rendering, and swap behavior.
Extend style/render-contract tests for the new roster-management panels and preference badges, while keeping existing tier-color and mobile-safe layout checks.
Run `npm test` and `npm run build` before handoff; run `npm run test:browser` only if a Chromium-family browser is available, and document whether it was executed or skipped.

risks.risk: Textarea content, current-match roster state, and saved-player state can drift apart if the app keeps multiple competing sources of truth.
risks.mitigation: Make `matchPlayers` the single canonical runtime state, and route paste hydration, saved-player load, and textarea serialization through shared helper functions.

risks.risk: Role preference controls can produce invalid or duplicated role orders, which will make preference badges inconsistent.
risks.mitigation: Centralize preference normalization in one helper, constrain UI control options, and add unit tests for all duplicate-order edge cases.

risks.risk: `localStorage` can be unavailable or contain corrupted JSON, causing startup crashes in a static frontend.
risks.mitigation: Wrap all storage access in safe load/save helpers that fall back to an empty store and show a non-blocking Korean warning instead of throwing.

risks.risk: Adding preference metadata to candidates can accidentally change comparison keys or ranking behavior.
risks.mitigation: Keep preference fields separate from the existing balance metric comparison path and lock the required ranking order with optimizer regression tests.

risks.risk: The compact preview area can become cluttered if preference information is rendered too aggressively.
risks.mitigation: Keep detailed editing controls in the current-roster and saved-player panels, and use only small badges or a short summary inside candidate cards.

risks.risk: The existing fake DOM harness is too limited for checkbox, select, and storage-heavy flows, which can leave regressions untested.
risks.mitigation: Upgrade the fake DOM early in the implementation and keep most preference/storage logic in pure helper modules that are easy to unit test.

risks.risk: Stored tier data and newly pasted tier data for the same player may conflict and confuse the update path.
risks.mitigation: Adopt one explicit rule: pasted tier values win for the current match, saved preference order is reused when available, and `현재 10명 저장/업데이트` writes the latest edited values back to storage.

definition_of_done: The existing paste, validation, 6-candidate preview, candidate selection, and two-click swap flow still works.
Users can edit per-player role preference order in-app without changing the clipboard format.
Role preference state is visible in candidate/editor assignments and updates correctly after candidate changes and swaps.
Users can save player tiers and preferences locally and later build a match by selecting exactly 10 saved players.
The required candidate ranking order and score-hidden UI rules remain intact.
The UI remains Korean-first, including all new preference and saved-player copy.
Automated tests cover preference logic, storage, saved-player loading, ranking preservation, candidate rendering, and swap recalculation, and `npm test` plus `npm run build` pass.
`README.md` and `FINAL_OUTPUT.md` accurately describe the shipped workflow and the non-blocking status of the older browser/mobile smoke gap.
open_questions: Assumption: the current compact-preview and swap-editor implementation is the baseline to extend, not something to replace wholesale.
Assumption: clipboard input stays at the existing 4 columns; role preferences are entered and edited in the app UI after paste or after loading saved players.
Assumption: default role preference order is derived from descending tier score, with ties resolved `tank -> damage -> support`.
Assumption: role preference is advisory fit metadata for candidate/editor display and manual editing, and it does not override the spec's mandatory balance sort order.
Assumption: saving the current roster upserts by normalized player name; delete/import/export management for saved players is out of scope for this iteration.
Assumption: loading saved players rewrites the textarea with a canonical header-included TSV so the visible input stays understandable to the user.
Assumption: if a pasted player already exists in storage, pasted tier values override saved tier values for the current match while saved preference order is reused unless the user edits it.
Assumption: the older real-browser/mobile QA gap remains documented but is intentionally non-blocking for this iteration unless a browser is available for optional smoke testing.
